Dual-backend consensus classification

Source: R/classify_dual.R
classify_variables_dual.Rd

Runs the deterministic rules classifier and the LLM pipeline independently on the same spec, then compares the two translations per variable at `ir_fingerprint(level = "full")` - complete canonical semantics, with registry defaults filled and intermediate names alpha-renamed, so a rule's `EXST_TRTSDTM` temp and an LLM's `EXSTDTM` compare equal when the derivation means the same thing.

Agreement adopts the rules IR (deterministic precedence; the semantics are identical anyway). Any divergence - different canonical semantics, or exactly one side abstaining - escalates the variable to `needs_human` with a rationale naming both layer chains. No side is ever silently preferred: a dual run never derives a variable that a rules-only run would have refused, and never accepts an LLM answer the rules disagreed with. Agreement is corroboration, not proof of correctness.

Usage

classify_variables_dual(
  spec,
  dataset,
  chat,
  samples = 1,
  prompt_variant = c("full", "neutral", "minimal")
)

Arguments

spec

Spec data frame compatible with [read_spec_df()].

dataset

Dataset name to classify (e.g. `"ADSL"`).

chat

ellmer chat object (or any object with a `chat(prompt)` method) for the LLM side.

samples

Number of independent LLM pipeline runs, passed to [classify_variables_llm()]; `> 1` gives the LLM side its own internal majority vote before the cross-backend comparison.

prompt_variant

System prompt variant for the LLM side; see [classify_variables_llm()].

Value

List of `aa_variable_ir` objects, one per spec variable, with two attributes: `dual`, a data.frame with columns `variable`, `class` (`agree`, `disagree`, `rules_abstain`, `llm_abstain`), `rules_fp`, `llm_fp` (full fingerprints), `rules_layers`, `llm_layers` (layer chains), and `llm_suggestion` (whether the LLM side produced a candidate the reviewer can inspect); `agreement_rate`, the fraction of variables where both backends produced the same canonical semantics; and `llm_candidates`, a named list holding the LLM-side IR for every escalated variable that has one (the reviewer's starting point; never rendered or executed without a human decision).

Details

Classify spec variables with two independent backends

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Not executable without an LLM provider API key (ellmer chat object):
chat <- ellmer::chat_deepseek(model = "deepseek-chat")
ir <- classify_variables_dual(mock_spec_adsl(), "ADSL", chat)
dual_disagreements(ir) # review queue: every variable the backends split on
} # }
